# dtcloud_vm_volume_attachment (Resource)

Attaches an existing volume to a virtual machine.

The attachment is its own resource rather than a block on `dtcloud_vm` because it has its own lifecycle: a volume can be detached and re-attached elsewhere without touching either the machine or the volume. There is nothing to update -- only attach and detach -- so every argument forces replacement.

The resource ID is `<vm-id>:<volume-id>`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The volume and the machine each have their own resource; this is only the
# attachment between them, so the volume can be detached and re-attached
# elsewhere without either being rebuilt.
resource "dtcloud_vm_volume_attachment" "data" {
  vm_id     = dtcloud_vm.web.id
  volume_id = dtcloud_volume.data.id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `vm_id` (String) ID of the virtual machine to attach to.
- `volume_id` (String) ID of the existing volume to attach.

### Optional

- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `size` (Number) Size of the attached volume in GB.
- `storage_policy` (String) Storage policy / volume type of the attached volume.
- `volume_name` (String) Name of the attached volume.

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String)
- `delete` (String)

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
# <vm-id>:<volume-id>
terraform import dtcloud_vm_volume_attachment.data 4c9a1f37-8d25-4e60-b13f-6a7c2e5b9d88:8a4f2c15-6b93-4d0e-a7f1-2c5b8e9d3a66
```
